SYSTEMS PROGRAMMING AND MACHINE ORGANIZATION
Chapter 60 — From Source Code to Running Program
VERBATIM GRADUATE LECTURE TRANSCRIPT
Charles Dorner

SLIDE 1: Chapter 60 — From Source Code to Running Program

LECTURE NARRATION
The previous chapters examined individual layers. This chapter follows one small program through the complete path: source text becomes instructions, the executable becomes mappings, instructions access translated memory, and I/O requests cross into the kernel. Each layer contributes a different kind of correctness and a different class of failure. The example computes a byte count and an unsigned 64-bit byte sum from standard input. The sum is intentionally simple and wraps modulo 2^64 ; the count rejects overflow rather than wrapping. Neither result is a cryptographic integrity guarantee. The simple operation makes the surrounding system behavior easy to inspect.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the previous chapters examined individual layers.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 4: 60.1 Source Code → Compiler

LECTURE NARRATION
Source code describes behavior under a language standard. Declarations establish types and interfaces; definitions provide objects and function bodies. The preprocessor handles includes and macros before the compiler’s language analysis. The compiler must reason about the program’s allowed behavior, including integer rules, object lifetime, aliasing, and observable effects. A pointer-and-length interface carries preconditions even when its machine representation is only two integer-like values. Invalid source-level behavior is not repaired by the fact that the target CPU can execute some corresponding instruction sequence. [ R1 , R8 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, source code describes behavior under a language standard.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 6: 60.2 Compiler → Assembly

LECTURE NARRATION
The compiler lowers the program into target instructions and chooses registers, branches, addressing modes, and transformations. The source loop need not survive as one literal assembly loop; optimization may unroll or vectorize it while preserving required behavior. The unsigned byte sum permits reassociation under modular arithmetic in ways that a strict floating-point sum might not. Numeric semantics therefore influence available machine implementations. Compare generated assembly only after identifying which transformations the source contract permits. [ R2 , R3 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the compiler lowers the program into target instructions and chooses registers, branches, addressing modes, and transformations.

SLIDE 8: 60.3 Assembly → Object Code

LECTURE NARRATION
The assembler encodes instructions and data into a relocatable object file. Symbols identify definitions and references, while relocation records describe locations that need adjustment when final addresses are determined. An object file is not yet necessarily a runnable executable. A call to checksum_update can refer to a symbol whose final location is unresolved until linking. Debug information and symbol tables help tools explain the relationship between source and machine code without being the code’s runtime semantics themselves.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the assembler encodes instructions and data into a relocatable object file.

SLIDE 10: 60.4 Object Code → Linker

LECTURE NARRATION
The linker combines object files and resolves symbols against other objects and libraries. It lays out the resulting program according to the executable format and link options. Missing definitions, incompatible interfaces, and duplicate definitions appear at this boundary. The C declaration and definition must agree. A successful link does not prove that a mismatched manually declared ABI is correct, and linking a library does not prove that its runtime dependencies will be available. Build correctness includes the intended headers, object versions, options, and target architecture. [ R1 , R37 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the linker combines object files and resolves symbols against other objects and libraries.

SLIDE 12: 60.5 Executable → Loader

LECTURE NARRATION
Execution asks the operating system to replace a process image with the executable. The kernel validates and interprets the executable format and establishes the initial execution environment. Dynamically linked programs also involve a runtime linker or loader according to the platform’s format and configuration. main is not normally the very first instruction executed. Startup code establishes language-runtime state before calling it. Understanding this explains why a program can fail before reaching the first source line of main , for example when a required dynamic library cannot be loaded. [ R16 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, execution asks the operating system to replace a process image with the executable.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 14: 60.6 Loader → Virtual Address Space

LECTURE NARRATION
The executable’s loadable segments become virtual mappings with appropriate permissions and backing. Code, initialized data, zero-filled storage, stack, and libraries occupy regions of the process’s address space. The loader need not eagerly copy every executable byte into physical memory before execution begins. File-backed demand paging and shared mappings allow work to occur as pages are used. The address-space layout is therefore a mapping plan, not simply a complete physical-memory photograph. [ R10 , R14 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
Think of an address written on a note: the note can tell you where to look, but it does not prove the thing is still there or that you are allowed to use it.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 16: 60.7 Instructions → CPU

LECTURE NARRATION
The processor fetches and executes instructions according to the ISA. Its microarchitecture can decode, schedule, speculate, and overlap operations while preserving the architectural behavior required for correct execution. The instruction pointer and registers describe the architectural stream, while internal execution details determine performance. A branch, cache miss, or dependency can change how quickly the next useful result becomes available without changing the program’s specified output. [ R3 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the processor fetches and executes instructions according to the ISA.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 18: 60.8 CPU → Registers and Caches

LECTURE NARRATION
The byte-sum loop uses registers for pointers, counters, and partial results where the compiler chooses. Loads obtain input bytes through the cache hierarchy. Several adjacent bytes can share a fetched line, giving spatial locality. Calling the update function may require arguments in the ABI’s designated registers and preservation of callee-saved state. Inlining can remove that call boundary but not the source-level requirement to read only valid input bytes. Machine optimization and memory safety remain separate obligations.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
A cache is like keeping the things you use most often on your desk instead of walking to a storage room every time.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 20: 60.9 Cache → Main Memory

LECTURE NARRATION
A cache miss obtains data from another level. Main memory backs the buffer’s resident pages, while translation hardware supplies the virtual-to-physical relationship. TLB misses, data-cache misses, and page faults remain distinct events even within this one loop. The loop’s sequential traversal can use cache lines efficiently, but the total throughput also depends on how input reaches the buffer. If the producer or storage source is slow, arithmetic optimization may have little effect on end-to-end completion time.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SLIDE 22: 60.10 Program → System Call

LECTURE NARRATION
The program calls read to obtain input and write to emit its result. Library wrappers marshal arguments into the operating-system ABI and translate return conventions into the documented C interface. Every positive read result supplies an exact valid extent for the next checksum update. The program must not process the entire 4096-byte buffer when only 100 bytes were returned. This is where an I/O return value becomes a memory-safety boundary. [ R11 , R12 , R46 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the program calls read to obtain input and write to emit its result.

SLIDE 24: 60.11 System Call → Kernel

LECTURE NARRATION
The kernel resolves the descriptor, checks the request, and performs or waits for the relevant operation. Standard input may be a regular file, pipe, terminal, or another endpoint, so the same user code can trigger different kernel paths. A blocking read may let another task run, while a read satisfied from available data may return without switching processes. Kernel entry, blocking, and context switching are separate events. Error and short-progress results return responsibility to the program’s control flow.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the kernel resolves the descriptor, checks the request, and performs or waits for the relevant operation.

SLIDE 26: 60.12 Kernel → Hardware

LECTURE NARRATION
When necessary, kernel subsystems and drivers coordinate with storage or network hardware. Interrupts, DMA, device queues, and memory-management policy can participate below the user-visible read interface. A cached read need not reach a device at all. Conversely, a device operation can complete before the waiting application is scheduled again. The end-to-end result is produced by several cooperating layers whose internal timings differ. Measure at the boundary relevant to the application’s requirement rather than attributing every delay to the CPU instruction loop.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, when necessary, kernel subsystems and drivers coordinate with storage or network hardware.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 28: Worked example — Build and trace a complete byte-summary utility

LECTURE NARRATION
The public interface states that data designates at least length valid bytes whenever length is nonzero. The function borrows the bytes and retains no pointer. Companion listing: ch60/checksum.h Companion listing: ch60/checksum.c Companion listing: ch60/main.c From the chapter’s source directory, the following commands expose separate stages. They write only local build products; use a copy or dedicated build directory for experimentation. The final output is bytes=4 sum=208 . The shell starts a producer and connects it to the utility through a pipe. The utility’s read returns valid bytes, the checksum function processes that exact extent, and a complete-transfer write emits the formatted result. A failure at any stage has a different meaning. Preprocessing can fail to find a header. Compilation can reject a type error. Linking can miss a definition. Loading can fail to locate a runtime dependency. Reading can fail on an invalid descriptor. The checksum itself can remain logically correct while the overall program fails to receive or deliver data. An integrated diagnosis identifies the failed boundary before changing unrelated code.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
Imagine several people editing the same whiteboard. If they do not coordinate, the final answer can depend on who writes at exactly the wrong moment.

SLIDE 30: Worked example — Following one global variable

LECTURE NARRATION
A source file defines int g=7; . The compiler emits code that refers to g and object-file data containing its initial value. The assembler encodes instructions and relocation records. The linker assigns g a location in the executable image. The loader maps the appropriate segment, and machine instructions later access the mapped bytes through virtual-memory translation and caches.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a source file defines int g=7; .

SLIDE 32: Worked example — Following one write system call

LECTURE NARRATION
Source code calls write(fd,p,n) . A library wrapper arranges arguments according to the ABI and executes the system-call entry instruction. The CPU transfers to kernel mode, where the kernel validates the descriptor and user buffer, updates kernel/device state, and returns a byte count or error. User-mode code resumes with the result. This single operation crosses language, ABI, ISA, kernel, and hardware boundaries.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, source code calls write(fd,p,n) .

SLIDE 34: Guided lab and review

LECTURE NARRATION
Lab 60. Build the two source files separately, omit checksum.o once to observe the controlled link failure, then restore it. Compare the sequential utility’s output for empty, text, binary, and multi-buffer input. Inspect loadable segments without assuming their virtual addresses are fixed across runs. Review 1. Why is main not necessarily the first executed code? Review 2. Which value determines how many buffer bytes the checksum may read after one system call?

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. SLIDE 36: Chapter Synthesis

LECTURE NARRATION
The chapter's central subject is from source code to running program. Correct reasoning requires explicit assumptions, bounds, ownership, and interface contracts. Observed behavior is evidence about a run; it is not automatically a language or system guarantee. Use the worked examples and lab to test whether the model transfers to new cases.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, the chapter's central subject is from source code to running program.
